newsitem.title: JAPAN: Rise in Japan surplus unlikely to be issue -- MOF.
newsitem.headline: Rise in Japan surplus unlikely to be issue -- MOF.

text.p: The rise in Japan's trade surplus is temporary and it is unlikely to become a major issue with other countries, Finance Minister Hiroshi Mitsuzuka told a news conference on Tuesday.
"The rapid weakening of the yen has brought about this (the rise in the trade surplus). However, this is a temporary increase," he said.
He added that the Group of Seven (G7) agreement on foreign exchange rates was filtering through to the markets.
Japan's trade surplus was unlikely to become a major issue since Japan was carrying out various deregulation and reform measures in the medium to longer term, he said.

Asked about reports that an official of Japan's ruling Liberal Democratic Pary was suggesting a rise in the official disocunt rate, Mitsuzuka said: "I know that some people hold such an opinion. However, interest rate decisions are up to the Bank of Japan. It is as the BOJ governor has been saying in parliament," he said.

Asked about a raid by Tokyo prosecutors on the headquarters of Dai-Ichi Kangyo Bank Ltd, Mitsuzuka said he had heard that the investigation was being carried out but did not know the details. "The Finance Ministry will keep watch over the investigation and deal with it appropriately," he said.
He also said he would reveal the amount of problem loans held by Nippon Credit Bank Ltd after an inspection of the bank is completed by the ministry.
